text: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise takes the caller identity from the session, the capability area, the right, the case and treatment reference, the field IDs the screen will show and the case attributes the scope test needs (owner, queue and team), and answers with the decision code (AC-READ or AC-DENY), the matrix version, the masking answer per field ID, the scope result and the access-entry reference.
why: Architecture v5 names the authorise operation and the TSD appendix does not, so the request and answer HAVE to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them empty would stop the story.
read: Arch v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 T-A.1 and T6.2; FSD P4 A2.4 and A2.7; Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 10 and 12
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 and 11; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build steps 1 and 2
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access tech lead when RWB-P4-E1037-CON is published
impact: A different shape changes the controller, the contract fake and every caller's client only; the decision codes, the entry and the messages stay as specified.

text: The rwb-access database login keeps the service naming convention (schema rwb_access with one login) and is named 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' in the story until the platform DB story fixes the name; no other REST path is added by this slice.
why: The legacy story names no login and the platform DB story has not fixed the per-service login names, and the story must not invent a credential name or a path.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 10 and 13; Arch v5 slides 14, 20 and 41; DP-02, DP-13
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 10 Authority; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Platform DB owner and the rwb-access tech lead, before the first migration runs
impact: Placeholder only; no behaviour depends on the literal name, and the grant model and the API surface are unchanged.

text: The booking-confirmation policy pack slice is read as the matrix version in force: TREATMENT_AND_OFFER R and CASE_RECORD R and U for RW-RESTRUCT and RW-CREDITAD, PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION U for RW-PLATADM, no PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION row for RW-CASEOWN, and scope ALL for RW-AUDIT, with no masking row because the screens show case IDs, treatment IDs, amounts and dates only.
why: The TSD RBAC matrix has no Case record or Treatment and offer column, while the legacy authority table and the task paths need those letters, so the letters are read from the pack as data rather than from a table.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4, 10 and 15; FSD P4 A2.4, A2.5 and A2.7; TSD P4 T3.1, T3.2 and T6.1; design charter of this slice
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Background and AC1 to AC6; section 8 Business rules BR5; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Matrix owner (RW-SECADM) and the P4 business analyst before PM-2026.12 goes in force
impact: If a letter differs, one row of the pack changes and no code changes; the default-deny rule keeps the refusal safe in the meantime.

text: An authorise decision is cached for the lifetime held as a parameter of the parameters contract and only under the matrix version it was decided on; a change of the pack version drops the cached entry in the transaction that writes the new version, so no restart is needed and no answer cached under the old version is served after the change.
why: Architecture v5 says the decision is cached and no source gives the lifetime, so the story fixes the version-keyed behaviour as a default and leaves the clock to a parameter.
read: Arch v5 slides 14 and 20; DP-06, DP-11; TSD P4 T6.2; Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 12
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 3 and 12; section 7 AC7; section 12.4 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data and Build step 6
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-access tech lead at the wave 2 design review
impact: A different lifetime changes one parameter value; the version-keyed drop and the entry are unaffected.

text: The authorise call for a payment-matching read carries the capability area (WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING or TREATMENT_AND_OFFER), the right R, the caller's resolved scope, the resource identifier, the filter, the row count of the answer the caller is about to return, and the matrix version to apply; the three answers are allow, refuse by right and refuse by scope.
why: The architecture names the call and three fields only (role, scope, DoA), while the access log has to hold the area, the right, the filter and the count for AC1, AC3, AC5 and AC8 to be provable.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 and its notes; TSD P4 v3 T6.2; FSD P4 v3 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 and AC-ALT-P4-007-02
confirm: Solution architect and the P4 contract owner at the RWB-P4-E1037-CON review for wave 2
impact: If the envelope differs, the request fixture, the entries and AC1, AC3 and AC5 change; the decision and the access-log rule do not.

text: The permission letters of the two capability areas are taken from the authority table of legacy RWB-E2-008: WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING R for RW-CREDITAD and for SY-AGENT, TREATMENT_AND_OFFER R for RW-CASEOWN, no WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING row for RW-CASEOWN, and R with scope ALL for RW-AUDIT; the default scope value of RW-CREDITAD is read from role.default_scope on the matrix version in force and is fixed nowhere in the story.
why: The TSD P4 T6.1 matrix covers three capability areas and gives RW-CASEOWN and RW-CREDITAD identical letters, which cannot be true here because the proceeds list must refuse the case owner.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE; FSD P4 v3 A2.4; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 10
confirm: Security administrator and the business lead when the 14-area matrix is published
impact: If the published letters differ, the policy-pack rows and the expected answers in AC1 to AC4 and AC7 change; no code changes, because the rows are data.

text: The AC-READ and AC-DENY entries carry the capability area, the right, the matrix version and, for a list or export read, the filter and the row count in the actions list of the decision-record entry, with no case ID on a list read; a single-record read records the case ID.
why: FSD P4 A2.7 requires the filter and the count to be logged and the decision record is the only log allowed in this run, but the LDM field set names neither.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01, AC-ALT-P4-007-02, AC-EXC-P4-007-04; TSD P4 v3 T6.3; LDM v8 DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018
confirm: Solution architect and the decision-record library owner in the next LDM version
impact: If the entry carries the values elsewhere, only the entry assertions of AC1, AC3 and AC8 change; the decision codes stay AC-READ and AC-DENY.

text: A caller with no permission row in the area, a dash for the right, or an environment with no matrix version in force is refused and never defaulted to allowed; the cached permission data is dropped when AccessPolicyChanged is published, so a changed matrix takes effect on the next call with no deployment; the access log is a decision-record entry and never a new Kafka event, and rwb-access publishes only AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged on rwb.access.events.v1.
why: The architecture makes AccessPolicyChanged a cache-refresh signal for every service and DP-03 makes the decision record the local log, while the legacy design wrote an access event; the refusal default and the refresh point have to be fixed for BR6, BR8 and BR10 to be testable.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43; TSD P4 v3 T4 and T5.3 (no events of its own); FSD P4 v3 A2.8; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03
applied_in: Sections 8 BR6, BR8, BR10; 12.3; 12.4; AC6, AC7, AC8
confirm: Solution architect and the event-platform owner, since no new topic is created
impact: If a separate access topic were required, AC8 and section 12.3 change and the Kafka platform story gains a topic; the default-refusal and refresh rules would stand.

text: GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits exists in rwb-access as Architecture v5 slide 14 names it and is added to the API Specification baseline with the field set this story writes; the API Specification v4 omission is a documentation defect, not a missing capability.
why: Architecture v5 outranks the API specification under R-PREC, and the ownership map cites API Specification v3 for the same operation with x_module P4.
read: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 14 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
confirm: API Specification owner, P4 business analyst
impact: If the operation is not confirmed the approval router has no DoA read and the key's routing cannot be built.

text: The lookup takes decisionCode, regulationItem, productGroup, principal, lossPct, lossAmount, pricePctFmv, relatedParty and onDate, and answers level, delegationLimitId, limitVersion, holderUserId, substituteUserId and outcome; the authority decision takes decisionCode, capability area, requiredLevel or routeRole and answers authorised, requiredLevel and outcome.
why: FSD A2.6 fixes only the level, the row and the version, and no source publishes the query or the payload; the story must name them to be buildable.
read: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.6; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 013 Approval routing with the delegation of authority table v1.md section 12
confirm: API Specification owner, P4 business analyst, P7 technical lead
impact: A renamed field changes the contract fake, the caller and the test data of both the P4 and the P7 slice.

text: The rwb-decision service identity holds Approval check R in rwb-access and nothing else, and GET /doa-limits and the DoA part of POST /authorise require that right; any other caller is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002.
why: No source names the identity or its rights, and the story cannot run an authorisation check without one.
read: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 14 and 41; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.1
confirm: Security administrator, P4 technical lead
impact: A wider or narrower scope changes the permission data and the denial test of section 16.

text: The access log of rwb-access is a decision-record entry of the local library of DP-03, one per lookup and one per authority decision, with decision codes AC-READ and AC-DENY, and there is no separate access-log table in rwb_access.
why: FSD P4 A2.7 and A2.8 put access events into the same append-only log as decisions and the pattern table makes that log the decision-record library; no source names an access decision code beyond AC-READ, AC-EXPT and AC-DENY.
read: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.7 and A2.8; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5 DP-03
confirm: P4 technical lead, internal audit
impact: If a separate access-log projection is required the story gains a table and a write path that the pattern table does not have.

text: The authorise request carries the actor user reference, the resolved roles, the capability area, the right, the object reference and, for an approval action, the route role; the response carries allowed, the roles that carry the right, the area, the right, the matrix version, the masking version, the field markers and a messageId.
why: Architecture v5 names POST /authorise and its purpose only, and TSD P4 v3 defines no authorise operation, so the story needs a shape to build and test against.
read: Arch v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 AC-ALT-P4-004-02 (a refusal names the area and the right)
confirm: P4 solution architect, at the contract review of RWB-P4-E1037-CON
impact: No field of the assumed shape is a business value; if the published shape differs, only the controller and the tests change, and no rule moves

text: The masked rendering of the addressee postal address is left to the one platform masking library and is not fixed by this story; the story asserts only that the field is marked masked, that the mask version is named, and that no value of the address appears in the answer or the access-log entry.
why: No source gives a mask format for a postal address and the story must not invent a business value.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule; FSD P4 v3 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05; LDM v8 DF-PTY-016
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, at the masking pack review
impact: A screen test that expects a format would fail until the format is data; the no-value assertion holds either way

text: The masking version in force for SIT is MASK-SIT-01, as the two FSD examples name it; the story reads the version from the masking rows at run time and configures no version.
why: No environment or load record states the masking version in force, and the story cannot invent a version label.
read: FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-05; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-202
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer with the P4 build squad, at the SIT entry check
impact: If SIT carries another masking version the tests read it from the rows; only the fixture label in the test data changes

text: The notice and approval facts reach rwb-access inside the authorise request from the composite route and from rwb-decision, and the cache refresh is driven by this service's own rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1; rwb-access consumes no other service's event and calls rwb-decision on this path.
why: Architecture v5 makes REST one hop with a 2 s timeout and lists AccessPolicyChanged as the cache-refresh trigger for every holder of permission data, but no source says how the approval facts reach the authorise call.
read: Arch v5 slide 14, slide 42 (AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged -> cache refresh) and the one-hop rule; TSD P4 v3 T5.2 and T5.3
confirm: P4 solution architect and the gateway-bff route owner, at the contract review
impact: Keeps this slice free of a synchronous dependency on rwb-decision; if the route instead passes only an object reference, the route makes the extra call and this service still reads no other service's table

text: The authorise request carries the object attributes the decision needs: the case ID, its team, its owner, and the escalated role and escalated time of an open SERVICE_LEVEL timer.
why: No source fixes the request payload, and the escalation grant of REQ-WKM-004 cannot be decided without those attributes crossing the boundary.
read: Architecture v5 slide 14 (POST /authorise role, scope, DoA); FSD P4 A2.14; ownership map (case and timer to P3)
confirm: Solution architect at the RWB-P4-E1037-CON contract review
impact: If the attributes differ, the request shape and the escalation rule change; the scope and masking rules stand

text: When the caller's own scope and an escalation grant both admit the case, the answer names the wider scope and carries the reason ESCALATED_TO_ROLE while the escalation is open.
why: The precedence is not specified and an answer has to name one scope.
read: FSD P4 A2.14; R-UNI-30; legacy RWB-E2-015 AC4
confirm: Business lead with the access policy owner
impact: The answer text and the audit reading of an escalated read; no case changes

text: MASK-SIT-01 is the masking version in force for the SIT environment, and the version whose valid_from is the latest on or before the business date is the version an answer uses.
why: The source names MASK-SIT-01 only in an exception path and gives no in-force rule for a version.
read: FSD P4 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer at the policy pack load
impact: A wrong default would show a personal field clear; the story would then ship the wrong masking version

text: RW-SPECIAL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD and RW-LEGAL keep the default scope their role row carries, since the source names Case record R for them without a scope.
why: The five access decisions of the legacy story name four roles with a right and no scope, and a scope answer is required.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-015 section 10; FSD P4 A2.4; TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE
confirm: Business lead with the security administrator
impact: Which cases those four roles may read; no masking and no audit change
